summary: Tonga's Ministry of Revenue and Customs lists the citizens of 53 countries and territories (as of 7 October 2026) who may be issued a 30-day visitor visa on arrival — among them the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and Ireland — provided they hold a valid return ticket and sufficient funds. Citizens of the 26 EU member states covered by the EU–Tonga visa waiver agreement (every member except Ireland) are visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period. Chinese citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, for less than 30 days. Citizens of every other country need a visa before arrival.

tips.text: The UK government says Tongan people strictly observe the Sabbath, and that on Sundays recreational activities may be considered disrespectful, except at island resorts.

The UK government says topless sunbathing and public nudity are illegal, with fines of up to 100 pa'anga, and that swimwear is acceptable on the beach or by streams and waterfalls but likely to attract negative attention elsewhere.

The UK government says it is illegal to swim or kayak with whales unless you are on a licensed boat with a certified guide, with fines of up to 5,000 pa'anga or 18 months in prison. Whales are in Tongan waters between June and November.

The UK government says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May but cyclones can happen at any time, and that Tonga lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions can trigger tsunamis.
Canada's travel advice says ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and that currency exchange may be limited on other islands.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tonga?
faq.answer: Not in advance if your country is on Tonga's list: citizens of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Singapore, Ireland and the other listed countries may be issued a 30-day visitor visa on arrival. Citizens of the 26 EU member states covered by the EU–Tonga visa waiver agreement need no visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Chinese citizens are visa-free under a bilateral agreement, for less than 30 days. Citizens of every other country — including South Korea, Israel, Iceland and Liechtenstein — must obtain a visa before arrival.

faq.question: How long is the visa on arrival valid for?
faq.answer: 30 days. Tonga's Ministry of Revenue and Customs issues it on condition of a valid return ticket out of Tonga and sufficient funds, and requires a passport valid for at least 6 months on entry; the UK Foreign Office says you may also need to show confirmed accommodation. To stay longer, contact the Immigration Department before the visa expires.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Tonga?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply to the Immigration Department in Nuku'alofa (Salote Road) or Neiafu, Vava'u, before your current visa expires. No official source publishes how long an extension lasts or the maximum total stay.

faq.question: Is everything really closed on Sunday in Tonga?
faq.answer: The UK government says Tongan people strictly observe the Sabbath and that recreational activities on Sundays may be seen as disrespectful, except at island resorts; Canada says such activity outside resorts may be seen as provocative.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Tonga?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says most major hotels and some restaurants and stores accept credit cards, ATMs are available on Tongatapu, especially in Nuku'alofa, and foreign currency exchange may be limited on other islands.
